title: Final rule to modify the enhanced supplementary leverage ratio standards
summary: On November 5, 2025, Federal Reserve staff presented a final rule for Board approval that would modify enhanced Supplementary Leverage Ratio (eSLR) standards for U.S. Global Systemically Important Bank Holding Companies (GSIBs) and their subsidiary depository institutions. The rule, to be issued jointly with FDIC and OCC upon completion of approval processes, would reduce eSLR buffer requirements to half of each GSIB's method 1 surcharge, with the stated goal of ensuring leverage ratios serve as backstops rather than binding constraints, thereby reducing disincentives for market intermediation activities that support Treasury market functioning.
key_points: Final rule modifies eSLR buffer standard for GSIBs to equal 50% of the method 1 surcharge under the Board's GSIB surcharge framework
For subsidiary depository institutions of GSIBs, eSLR standard becomes a buffer equal to 50% of parent GSIB's method 1 surcharge, capped at 1%
Rule reduces likelihood that supplementary leverage ratio requirements are the binding capital constraint for GSIBs and their subsidiaries
Effective date is April 1, 2026; early adoption permitted beginning January 1, 2026
Issued jointly by Board of Governors, FDIC, and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
Conforming changes made to Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) and long-term debt requirements
Rule aims to reduce disincentives for GSIB-affiliated broker-dealers to intermediate in U.S. Treasury markets
Minimum supplementary leverage ratio remains 3% for Category I-III capital standards; eSLR leverage buffer currently 2%
why_it_matters: This proposed regulatory change, pending final approval, directly affects how GSIBs manage their balance sheets and their capacity to provide market-making and intermediation services in Treasury markets. By reducing the likelihood that leverage requirements are binding, the agencies aim to encourage GSIBs to engage in lower-risk, lower-return activities like Treasury market intermediation. This could support market resilience and liquidity, particularly in stressed conditions. For market participants, this represents a potential structural change in bank behavior incentives that could affect Treasury market depth and bid-ask spreads. Effective date is April 1, 2026.
market_structure_context: The rule explicitly addresses market structure concerns related to Treasury market functioning. The agencies note that binding leverage requirements can create incentives for firms to reduce participation in market intermediation activities. By calibrating eSLR standards to serve as backstops rather than binding constraints, the rule aims to support the smooth functioning of the U.S. Treasury market where GSIBs play an important intermediation role. The rule modifies capital requirements that affect broker-dealer market-making capacity in Treasury markets.
important_numbers: 6% minimum supplementary leverage ratio for insured depository institution subsidiaries to be 'well capitalized'
50% (proposed eSLR buffer as percentage of method 1 surcharge)
1% cap on subsidiary depository institution eSLR buffer
